correctness.rationale: The normalization for λ=2,μ=3 is 2 N(2x+3y) N(3x−2y)/[13(N(x)^2+N(y)^2)]. Each norm is max over eight signed support functionals. Choose active supports c,d; every 64 ordered pair of normals reduces under dihedral symmetries to five angular relative classes k=0..4. For each class the package specifies positive convex combinations G_x,G_y of rank-one normal projections, hence x^TG_x x≤N(x)^2 and similarly y. The proposed 4×4 symmetric matrix C0 diag(G_x,G_y)−(ell m^T+m ell^T)/2, C0=3+149√2/48, is PSD for all five classes. I independently reconstructed these matrices and all 75 nonempty principal minors: 26 identically zero, 49 strictly positive using exact rational comparisons in Q(√2), so PSD is mathematically certified independent of numerical scanning. Independently recomputed the witness x=(1−√2,−1), y=(−z,−w), z=6/(9+4√2), w=(9−4√2−6z)/12; direct active-support evaluation gives N(x)=1, N(y)=z, exactly the claimed quotient (144+149√2)/312. A finite set of certificates is exhaustive because every possible active support pair reduces to one of the five proven classes; no assumption about sampled vectors is used.
residual_risks: The 4×4 PSD certificate is tied to the fixed octagon norm and (2,3), not all λ,μ.

value.rationale: The exact generalized Zbăganu product invariant for the regular octagon at the defining paper’s natural λ,μ=(2,3) is a motivated benchmark bridging Hilbert (value 1) and square-type extremal endpoints. A complete global exact certificate across 64 active-support pairs and a sharp algebraic witness are nontrivial, independently reusable tools for related polyhedral Banach-space constants. The fixed parameter pair is not arbitrary: it is explicitly singled out by the initiating 2021 Example 4.3.
residual_risks: Does not classify other parameter pairs, polygonal norms, or all optimizers.
